items.title: LSP verifier registry and execution contract
items.statement: LspGateVerifier is registered under an LSP verification method without changing the gate runner flow, obtains diagnostics for resolved paths through the LSP client API, and returns the standard VerifierResult shape.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LspGateVerifier is registered in VerifierRegistry under lsp or lsp_gate verification_method, runs without changing gate_runner flow, calls the LSP client diagnostics API for resolved paths, and returns VerifierResult with passed, message, and evidence.

items.title: Verification method alias resolution is ambiguous
items.statement: The registry key is expressed as 'lsp or lsp_gate', but the authoritative unit does not say whether both values are required aliases, which is canonical, or how collisions and unknown values are handled.
items.impact: Implementations can register or dispatch different method identifiers and become configuration-incompatible.
items.builder_discretion: Choose whether to register one or both identifiers and choose alias precedence or collision behavior.

items.title: Verification configuration and evidence wiring
items.statement: VerificationConfig gains nested lsp_gate configuration; enabled tier boundaries inject LSP criteria, method dispatch executes them, and results use the existing evidence and GateReport aggregation without a new GateReport field.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Implementer wiring extends VerificationConfig with nested lsp_gate, injects lsp criteria at enabled tier boundaries, dispatches by verification method, and uses existing evidence and GateReport aggregation without adding a new GateReport field.

items.title: Nested lsp_gate configuration contract is not typed or defaulted
items.statement: The unit preserves names for enabled, scope, block_on, tier_boundaries, timeout_seconds, and when_unavailable, but does not define their types, defaults, allowed values, validation, or exact tier-injection mapping.
items.impact: Config producers, persistence, gate construction, and verifier dispatch can disagree on accepted data and runtime behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Define the nested schema, defaults, validation errors, tier matching, timeout behavior, and unavailable-server behavior.

items.title: Verification tab persists LSP gate controls in the shared settings blob
items.statement: The user-visible Verification tab binds its LSP diagnostics gate controls to nested lsp_gate configuration and persists those values in the existing verification settings blob.

items.impact: UI implementations can expose different settings and persistence or error behavior despite satisfying the broad binding sentence.
items.builder_discretion: Design the concrete controls, state dependencies, validation, error messaging, and persistence interaction.

items.title: Prompt evidence auto-ingestion cap
items.statement: Prompt assembly may automatically ingest no more than five currently most relevant or severe LSP/debug evidence items; excess material is summary-only unless the user opens the full runtime artifact.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Prompt-consumable LSP/debug evidence may auto-ingest at most the top five evidence items by current relevance or severity; after that cap, additional diagnostics or trace material enter summarization-only mode unless the user explicitly opens the full runtime artifact.

items.title: Evidence ranking and summarization are non-deterministic
items.statement: The cap names relevance or severity but defines neither their ordering or combination nor tie-breaking, recency, deduplication, summary size, summary fidelity, or the effect of opening the artifact on subsequent prompt ingestion.
items.impact: Different builders can select different evidence, omit critical diagnostics, and produce materially different prompt context.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the ranking function, tie-breaks, lifecycle of relevance, summary algorithm and budget, and explicit-open semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Prompt-consumable LSP/debug evidence may auto-ingest at most the top five evidence items by current relevance or severity; after that cap, additional diagnostics or trace material enter summarization-only mode unless the user explicitly opens the full runtime artifact.

items.title: Diagnostic entry schema and severity vocabulary
items.statement: Each snapshot diagnostic contains path, line, character, severity, message, source, and optional code; severity values are exactly Error, Warning, Info, and Hint.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Each LSP evidence snapshot diagnostic entry stores path, line, character, severity, message, source, and optional code with severity values Error, Warning, Info, and Hint.

items.title: Diagnostic field types and invariants are absent
items.statement: The entry field names and severity vocabulary are fixed, but field data types, nullability beyond optional code, path normalization, message encoding, code representation, source semantics, and malformed-entry handling are not specified.
items.impact: Snapshot writers and readers can serialize incompatible JSON or interpret diagnostic locations differently.
items.builder_discretion: Define JSON types, requiredness, normalization, allowed nulls, and validation or rejection behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Each LSP evidence snapshot diagnostic entry stores path, line, character, severity, message, source, and optional code with severity values Error, Warning, Info, and Hint.

items.title: Line-coordinate conversion boundary
items.statement: Diagnostic line numbers are stored and displayed as 1-based values; they transition to 0-based values only while crossing the LSP protocol boundary and must not expose 0-based lines in evidence or UI.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP diagnostic evidence stores and displays line values as 1-based for evidence and UI while converting to 0-based only at the LSP protocol boundary.

items.title: Character-coordinate semantics are missing
items.statement: Diagnostics include a character field, but only line-number conversion is defined; character base, UTF-8 versus UTF-16 units, storage/display conversion, and invalid-position handling remain unspecified.
items.impact: Locations can point to the wrong character, especially for non-ASCII text, and clients can disagree on serialized evidence coordinates.
items.builder_discretion: Choose character indexing units and all boundary conversions and validation.

items.title: Snapshot lifecycle, atomicity, and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The plan fixes a directory and filename patterns but does not define directory creation, atomic writes, collision avoidance, overwrite policy, partial-write recovery, read corruption handling, retention, cleanup, or maximum artifact size.
items.impact: Concurrent or failed gate runs can lose, corrupt, overwrite, or indefinitely accumulate evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Select filesystem creation and permissions, atomic commit method, uniqueness mechanism, corruption recovery, retention, cleanup, and size limits.

items.impact: Artifacts can retain sensitive project paths and diagnostic contents or be exposed to unintended local or downstream consumers.

items.title: Verifier failure and recovery semantics are absent
items.statement: The verifier contract names resolved-path diagnostics and a passed/message/evidence result, but does not define behavior for unavailable clients, timeouts, unresolved or missing paths, partial diagnostic responses, protocol errors, cancellation, retries, or how those conditions map to passed, message, evidence, and block_on.
items.impact: The same infrastructure fault can be treated as pass, fail, block, retry, or empty evidence by different implementations, directly changing promotion decisions.
items.builder_discretion: Define error classes, retry and cancellation policy, partial-result policy, unavailable behavior, and deterministic VerifierResult and gate-blocking mappings.

dimension_assessments.summary: Registry execution, config injection, UI persistence, evidence capping, coordinate conversion, and snapshot storage behaviors are stated.
The core grants LSP gate verification, snapshot evidence, settings control, and bounded prompt-evidence consumption capabilities.
Verifier and snapshot outputs are named, but config and diagnostic schemas lack types, defaults, validation, and complete coordinate semantics.
Several contracts are explicit, but registry aliasing, configuration schema, diagnostic types, ranking, and failure mappings remain materially open.
The 1-based to 0-based line transition is explicit, while UI states, verifier failure states, prompt artifact-open transitions, and snapshot lifecycle transitions are undefined.
LSPSupport authority over LSP-specific protocol and client constraints is explicit and bounded by other owner documents' SSOT.
All covered PlanUnits name Plans/LSPSupport.md as owner and repeat the LSP-specific owner boundary.
Gate dispatch, GateReport and EvidenceStore aggregation, Verification tab persistence, evidence/UI display, snapshot readers, and prompt consumption surfaces are identifiable in the core.
Verification-tab binding and 1-based line display are explicit GUI truth, but concrete control and interaction states are not specified.
Unavailable-client, timeout, path, partial-response, protocol, persistence, and corrupted-snapshot behavior and recovery are not defined.
Persistent diagnostic and project-path evidence has no redaction, access, permission, retention, encryption, or export policy in the core.
Consumers are related by their text, but empty dependency and unblock declarations omit schema, config, UI, evidence, and prompt propagation ordering.
Snapshot destination and naming are stated, but filesystem creation, write atomicity, collision handling, cleanup, retention, and corruption recovery are absent.
A five-item prompt cap limits direct context, but ranking cost, summary budgets, diagnostic volume, snapshot size, concurrency, and retention limits remain unspecified.
Existing gate flow, criterion enum, GateReport, and settings blob are preserved, but dual method identifiers and untyped config evolution leave migration compatibility ambiguous.
Listed checks validate plan migration and indexing, not the runtime, UI, serialization, ranking, coordinate, or recovery behavior.
Consequential discretion remains in aliasing, config defaults and validation, UI interactions, evidence ranking, coordinate units, failures, snapshot operations, security, propagation, and tests.

The principal unknowns are registry key semantics, config schema and tier mapping, UI states, relevance-versus-severity ordering, character coordinates, artifact lifecycle, and infrastructure-error outcomes.
